source.text: כִּֽי־תֵצֵ֨א לַמִּלְחָמָ֜ה עַל־אֹיְבֶ֗יךָ וְֽרָאִ֜יתָ ס֤וּס וָרֶ֨כֶב֙ עַ֚ם רַ֣ב מִמְּךָ֔ לֹ֥א תִירָ֖א מֵהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ הַמַּֽעַלְךָ֖ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: When you go out to the battle against your enemies and you see horse and chariot, a people more numerous than you, not you shall be afraid of them, for Yahweh your God [is] with you, the [one] bringing you up from [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horse and chariot, a people more numerous than you, you shall not be afraid of them, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
en.B: When you march out to battle against your enemies and face horses and chariots and a force bigger than your own, do not fear them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
en.R: You will go out to fight your enemies, and you may see that they have horses and chariots and a bigger army than yours. Do not be afraid of them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is with you. He is the one who brought you out of Egypt.

es.L: Cuando salgas a la batalla contra tus enemigos y veas caballo y carro, un pueblo más numeroso que tú, no tendrás miedo de ellos, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios [está] contigo, el que te hizo subir de la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: Cuando marches a la guerra contra tus enemigos y te enfrentes a caballos, carros y un ejército más numeroso que el tuyo, no les tengas miedo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, que te sacó de la tierra de Egipto, está contigo.
es.R: Saldrás a pelear contra tus enemigos, y tal vez veas que tienen caballos y carros y un ejército más grande que el tuyo. No les tengas miedo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios está contigo. Él es quien te sacó de Egipto.

fr.L: Quand tu sortiras au combat contre tes ennemis et que tu verras cheval et char, un peuple plus nombreux que toi, tu n’auras pas peur d’eux, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu [est] avec toi, lui qui t’a fait monter du pays d’Égypte.
fr.B: Quand tu partiras en guerre contre tes ennemis et que tu te trouveras face à des chevaux, des chars et une armée plus nombreuse que la tienne, ne les crains pas. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, qui t’a fait monter du pays d’Égypte, est avec toi.
fr.R: Tu iras te battre contre tes ennemis, et tu verras peut-être qu’ils ont des chevaux, des chars et une armée plus grande que la tienne. N’aie pas peur d’eux. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est avec toi. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui t’a fait sortir d’Égypte.

sw.L: Utakapotoka kwenda vitani dhidi ya adui zako, na kuona farasi na gari la vita, watu wengi kuliko wewe, usiwaogope, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako [yu] pamoja nawe, aliyekupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri.
sw.B: Utakapotoka kwenda kupigana na adui zako, ukakutana na farasi na magari ya vita na jeshi kubwa kuliko lako, usiwaogope. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, aliyekupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, yuko pamoja nawe.
sw.R: Utakwenda kupigana na adui zako, na huenda ukaona kwamba wana farasi na magari ya vita na jeshi kubwa kuliko lako. Usiwaogope. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako yuko pamoja nawe. Yeye ndiye aliyekutoa Misri.

decisions.choice: the laws of war: how Israel is to go to battle
decisions.reason: This chapter gathers Moses' rules for war: who is sent home before a battle (verses 1-9), how a distant city is to be offered peace first (verses 10-15), the different command for the cities of the land itself (verses 16-18), and the sparing of fruit trees during a siege (verses 19-20). It speaks to the whole people as one "you".

decisions.choice: horse and chariot: horses and chariots, the enemy's chariot force
decisions.reason: Both nouns are singular, used for a whole class of things. Chariots drawn by horses were the strongest weapon of the armies around Israel, which Israel did not have (Joshua 11:4; 17:16; Judges 4:3).

decisions.choice: the God who brought you out of Egypt is with you: the past rescue is the ground for courage now
decisions.reason: God is named by what he did: he is "the one bringing you up" from Egypt. At the sea he overthrew Pharaoh's horses and chariots (Exodus 14:23-28; 15:1, 4), so Israel need not fear horses and chariots now. Moses gives the same reason against fear in 7:17-19.

decisions.choice: a force bigger than your own / a bigger army
decisions.reason: The word is "people", but here it means the enemy's fighting force, so Balanced says "force" and Readable "army".

decisions.choice: "tú" for Israel in the laws of war; the plural_you span only where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verses 2-4, 18)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses the whole people as one "you" (m1); Spanish follows its number at every level, as elsewhere in Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: "tu" for Israel in the laws of war; "vous" where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verses 2-4, 18)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses the whole people as one "you" (m1), and turns to the plural only in the priest's words and in verse 18; the French follows its number at every level, as elsewhere in Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: singular forms ("wewe", "Mungu wako") for Israel; plural forms ("ninyi", "-enu") in verses 2-4 and 18
decisions.reason: The Swahili follows the Hebrew number of "you" at every level, as elsewhere in Deuteronomy.

source.text: וְהָיָ֕ה כְּקָֽרָבְכֶ֖ם אֶל־הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִגַּ֥שׁ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְדִבֶּ֥ר אֶל־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, and shall come near the priest and speak to the people.

en.L: And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.
en.B: As you approach the battle, the priest is to step forward and speak to the troops.
en.R: Just before the battle begins, the priest must come forward and speak to the soldiers.

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando {{plural_you:se acerquen|os acerquéis}} a la batalla, el sacerdote se adelantará y hablará al pueblo.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} a punto de entrar en batalla, el sacerdote se adelantará y hablará a las tropas.
es.R: Justo antes de que empiece la batalla, el sacerdote debe adelantarse y hablar a los soldados.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand vous vous approcherez du combat, que le prêtre s’avancera et parlera au peuple.
fr.B: Au moment où vous approcherez du combat, le prêtre s’avancera et parlera aux troupes.
fr.R: Juste avant le début de la bataille, le prêtre doit s’avancer et parler aux soldats.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, mtakapoikaribia vita, kuhani atasogea mbele na kusema na watu.
sw.B: Mnapokaribia kuingia vitani, kuhani asogee mbele na kusema na wanajeshi.
sw.R: Kabla tu vita havijaanza, lazima kuhani asogee mbele na kusema na askari.

decisions.choice: the priest: a priest who goes out with the army
decisions.reason: A priest went with Israel's army to blow the trumpets and carry the holy things (Numbers 10:9; 31:6). His words before the battle remind the soldiers that the battle is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: the people: the men gathered for battle
decisions.reason: "The people" here, as in verses 5, 8 and 9, are the men called up to fight, the army of Israel.

decisions.choice: the troops / the soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people by their role in this setting. Literal keeps "people".

source.text: וְאָמַ֤ר אֲלֵהֶם֙ שְׁמַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּ֨ם קְרֵבִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־אֹיְבֵיכֶ֑ם אַל־יֵרַ֣ךְ לְבַבְכֶ֗ם אַל־תִּֽירְא֧וּ וְאַֽל־תַּחְפְּז֛וּ וְאַל־תַּֽעַרְצ֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he shall say to them, hear, Israel, you [are] drawing near today to the battle against your enemies; not let be faint your heart, not fear and not panic and not tremble before them,

en.L: And he shall say to them, 'Hear, Israel: you [are] drawing near today to battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart be faint; do not fear, and do not panic, and do not tremble before them,
en.B: He shall say to them, 'Hear, Israel: today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not shrink back in terror before them,
en.R: He must say to them, 'Listen, Israel! Today you are going to fight your enemies. Do not lose courage. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not be terrified of them.

es.L: Y les dirá: “Escucha, Israel: {{plural_you:ustedes se acercan|vosotros os acercáis}} hoy a la batalla contra {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}}. Que no desfallezca {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}}; no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}, no {{plural_you:se alarmen|os alarméis}} y no {{plural_you:tiemblen|tembléis}} delante de ellos,
es.B: Les dirá: “Escucha, Israel: hoy {{plural_you:van|vais}} a entrar en batalla contra {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}}. No {{plural_you:se desanimen|os desaniméis}}. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo, no {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} llevar por el pánico y no {{plural_you:retrocedan|retrocedáis}} aterrados ante ellos,
es.R: Les dirá: “¡Escucha, Israel! Hoy {{plural_you:van|vais}} a pelear contra {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}}. No {{plural_you:pierdan|perdáis}} el valor. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo, no {{plural_you:se asusten|os asustéis}} y no {{plural_you:se aterroricen|os aterroricéis}} ante ellos.

fr.L: Et il leur dira : “Écoute, Israël : vous vous approchez aujourd’hui du combat contre vos ennemis. Que votre cœur ne faiblisse pas ; ne craignez pas, ne vous affolez pas et ne tremblez pas devant eux,
fr.B: Il leur dira : “Écoute, Israël : aujourd’hui vous allez livrer bataille à vos ennemis. Ne perdez pas courage. N’ayez pas peur, ne vous affolez pas et ne reculez pas, saisis d’effroi, devant eux,
fr.R: Il doit leur dire : “Écoute, Israël ! Aujourd’hui vous allez combattre vos ennemis. Ne perdez pas courage. N’ayez pas peur, ne paniquez pas et ne soyez pas terrifiés devant eux.

sw.L: Naye atawaambia, 'Sikia, Israeli: ninyi mnakaribia leo vita dhidi ya adui zenu. Mioyo yenu isizimie; msiogope, wala msitaharuki, wala msitetemeke mbele yao,
sw.B: Atawaambia, 'Sikia, Israeli: leo mnakwenda vitani kupigana na adui zenu. Msife moyo. Msiogope, msitaharuki, wala msirudi nyuma kwa hofu kuu mbele yao,
sw.R: Lazima awaambie, 'Sikiliza, Israeli! Leo mnakwenda kupigana na adui zenu. Msipoteze ujasiri. Msiogope, msitaharuki, wala msiingiwe na hofu kuu mbele yao.

decisions.choice: Hear, Israel: the call that opens Moses' own teaching
decisions.reason: The priest begins with the words Moses uses to call the whole people to listen (5:1; 6:4; 9:1). Before battle the army is addressed as Israel, the LORD's people.

decisions.choice: let your heart be faint: lose courage
decisions.reason: The heart here is the seat of courage. A "soft" or faint heart is one that gives way in fear; verse 8 uses the same picture for the fearful man.

decisions.choice: fear, panic, tremble: three words for losing nerve
decisions.reason: The commands pile up for force. The second verb means to hurry off in alarm, as men do when they flee (1 Samuel 23:26; 2 Kings 7:15); the third means to shake with dread (1:29; 7:21; 31:6).

decisions.choice: lose heart / lose courage; shrink back in terror
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture "let your heart be faint". The last verb is the strongest of the three, so Balanced says "shrink back in terror" and Readable "be terrified".

decisions.choice: "Escucha, Israel", then the plural_you span
decisions.reason: The call to listen is singular, as in 6:4 and 9:1; the rest of the priest's words are plural, spoken to the soldiers. The Spanish keeps both numbers.

decisions.choice: "Écoute, Israël", then "vous"
decisions.reason: The call to listen is singular, as in 6:4 and 9:1, addressed to Israel as one people; what follows is plural, spoken to the men in the ranks. The French keeps both numbers.

source.text: כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם הַהֹלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּכֶ֑ם לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם עִם־אֹיְבֵיכֶ֖ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: for Yahweh your God [is] the [one] going with you to fight for you with your enemies, to save you.

en.L: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [is] the one who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.'
en.B: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the one who goes with you. He will fight for you against your enemies and give you victory.'
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going with you. He will fight your enemies for you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save you.'

es.L: porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} [es] el que va con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para pelear por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} contra {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}}, para {{plural_you:salvarlos|salvaros}}”.
es.B: porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} es el que va con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él peleará por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} contra {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} dará la victoria”.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} va con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él peleará contra {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}} en {{plural_you:su lugar|vuestro lugar}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} salvará”.

fr.L: car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu [est] celui qui marche avec vous, pour combattre pour vous contre vos ennemis, pour vous sauver.”
fr.B: car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu est celui qui marche avec vous. Il combattra pour vous contre vos ennemis et vous donnera la victoire.”
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu marche avec vous. Il combattra vos ennemis à votre place, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous sauvera.”

sw.L: kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu [ndiye] anayekwenda pamoja nanyi, ili kuwapigania dhidi ya adui zenu, ili kuwaokoa.'
sw.B: kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu ndiye anayekwenda pamoja nanyi. Atawapigania dhidi ya adui zenu na kuwapa ushindi.'
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anakwenda pamoja nanyi. Atapigana na adui zenu kwa ajili yenu, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawaokoa.'

decisions.choice: to fight for you: the LORD fights Israel's battles
decisions.reason: Moses says the same at the sea and in the wilderness: the LORD fights for his people (Exodus 14:14; Deuteronomy 1:30; 3:22). The courage asked for in verse 3 rests on this.

decisions.choice: to save you: to rescue you by giving you the victory
decisions.reason: The verb means to rescue from danger. In a battle that rescue is victory over the enemy (Judges 7:2; 1 Samuel 14:23).

decisions.choice: give you victory
decisions.reason: Balanced says what saving means in a battle; Literal and Readable keep "save". The priest's words close at the end of this verse.

source.text: וְדִבְּר֣וּ הַשֹּֽׁטְרִים֮ אֶל־הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹר֒ מִֽי־הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֤ה בַֽיִת־חָדָשׁ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֲנָכ֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן־יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יַחְנְכֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall speak the officials to the people, saying, who [is] the man who has built a house new and not dedicated it? Let him go and let him return to his house, lest he die in the battle and a man other dedicate it.

en.L: And the officials shall speak to the people, saying, 'Who [is] the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
en.B: Then the officials are to say to the troops, 'Has anyone built a new house and not yet dedicated it? He should go back home, or he may die in battle and someone else dedicate it.
en.R: Then the officials must say to the soldiers, 'Has any man here built a new house but not yet dedicated it? He should go back home. Otherwise he might die in the battle, and another man would dedicate his house.

es.L: Y los funcionarios hablarán al pueblo, diciendo: “¿Quién [es] el hombre que ha edificado una casa nueva y no la ha dedicado? Que se vaya y vuelva a su casa, no sea que muera en la batalla y otro hombre la dedique.
es.B: Luego los funcionarios dirán a las tropas: “¿Hay alguien que haya construido una casa nueva y todavía no la haya dedicado? Que vuelva a su casa, no sea que muera en la batalla y otro la dedique.
es.R: Después los funcionarios deben decir a los soldados: “¿Hay aquí algún hombre que haya construido una casa nueva y todavía no la haya estrenado? Que regrese a su casa. Si no, podría morir en la batalla, y otro hombre estrenaría su casa.

fr.L: Et les préposés parleront au peuple en disant : “Qui [est] l’homme qui a bâti une maison neuve et ne l’a pas inaugurée ? Qu’il s’en aille et retourne à sa maison, de peur qu’il ne meure au combat et qu’un autre homme ne l’inaugure.
fr.B: Puis les préposés diront aux troupes : “Quelqu’un a-t-il bâti une maison neuve sans l’avoir encore inaugurée ? Qu’il retourne chez lui, sinon il pourrait mourir au combat et un autre l’inaugurerait.
fr.R: Ensuite, les responsables doivent dire aux soldats : “Y a-t-il ici un homme qui a construit une maison neuve mais ne l’a pas encore inaugurée ? Qu’il rentre chez lui. Sinon, il pourrait mourir dans la bataille, et un autre homme inaugurerait sa maison.

sw.L: Na wasimamizi watasema na watu, wakisema, 'Ni nani mtu aliyejenga nyumba mpya, naye hajaiweka wakfu? Aende, arudi nyumbani kwake, asije akafa vitani, na mtu mwingine akaiweka wakfu.
sw.B: Kisha wasimamizi waseme na wanajeshi, 'Je, kuna mtu aliyejenga nyumba mpya na bado hajaiweka wakfu? Arudi nyumbani, asije akafa vitani na mtu mwingine akaiweka wakfu.
sw.R: Kisha lazima maafisa waseme na askari, 'Je, kuna mtu hapa aliyejenga nyumba mpya lakini bado hajaiweka wakfu? Arudi nyumbani. La sivyo, anaweza kufa vitani, na mtu mwingine ataiweka wakfu nyumba yake.

decisions.choice: the officials: officers who kept the records and carried out orders
decisions.reason: These are the officers set beside the judges in every town (1:15; 16:18). Here they muster the army and decide who goes home.

decisions.choice: dedicate a house: begin to live in it
decisions.reason: The verb is used for dedicating the altar (Numbers 7:10) and the temple (1 Kings 8:63). For a house it means its first use as a home; whether a ceremony went with it is not known.

decisions.choice: lest another man dedicate it: losing the fruit of one's labor
decisions.reason: To build a house and never live in it is one of the curses for breaking the covenant (28:30). This rule keeps a man from that loss. The same care stands behind the newly married man's year at home (24:5).

decisions.choice: who is the man ...?: an open call to anyone it fits
decisions.reason: The question works as "whoever ...": any man to whom it applies is to step forward and go home.

decisions.choice: Has anyone ...? He should go back home
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "who is the man" into a plain question and "let him go and return" into a plain instruction. Those sent home are soldiers, so Readable says "any man here".

decisions.choice: estrenado / estrenaría
decisions.reason: Dedicating a house meant beginning to live in it (m2). Readable uses the everyday "estrenar", to use something new for the first time; Literal and Balanced keep "dedicar".

source.text: וּמִֽי־הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־נָטַ֥ע כֶּ֨רֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א חִלְּל֔וֹ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן־יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יְחַלְּלֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And who [is] the man who has planted a vineyard and not begun to use it? Let him go and let him return to his house, lest he die in the battle and a man other begin to use it.

en.L: And who [is] the man who has planted a vineyard and has not put it to common use? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man put it to common use.
en.B: Has anyone planted a vineyard and not yet begun to enjoy its fruit? He should go back home, or he may die in battle and someone else enjoy it.
en.R: Has any man planted a vineyard but not yet eaten its grapes? He should go back home. Otherwise he might die in the battle, and another man would eat them.

es.L: ¿Y quién [es] el hombre que ha plantado una viña y no la ha puesto en uso común? Que se vaya y vuelva a su casa, no sea que muera en la batalla y otro hombre la ponga en uso común.
es.B: ¿Hay alguien que haya plantado una viña y todavía no haya empezado a disfrutar de su fruto? Que vuelva a su casa, no sea que muera en la batalla y otro la disfrute.
es.R: ¿Hay algún hombre que haya plantado una viña y todavía no haya comido sus uvas? Que regrese a su casa. Si no, podría morir en la batalla, y otro hombre se las comería.

fr.L: Et qui [est] l’homme qui a planté une vigne et ne l’a pas rendue à l’usage commun ? Qu’il s’en aille et retourne à sa maison, de peur qu’il ne meure au combat et qu’un autre homme ne la rende à l’usage commun.
fr.B: Quelqu’un a-t-il planté une vigne sans avoir encore commencé à en goûter le fruit ? Qu’il retourne chez lui, sinon il pourrait mourir au combat et un autre en profiterait.
fr.R: Y a-t-il un homme qui a planté une vigne mais n’a pas encore mangé de ses raisins ? Qu’il rentre chez lui. Sinon, il pourrait mourir dans la bataille, et un autre homme les mangerait.

sw.L: Na ni nani mtu aliyepanda shamba la mizabibu, naye hajalitumia kwa matumizi ya kawaida? Aende, arudi nyumbani kwake, asije akafa vitani, na mtu mwingine akalitumia kwa matumizi ya kawaida.
sw.B: Je, kuna mtu aliyepanda shamba la mizabibu na bado hajaanza kufurahia matunda yake? Arudi nyumbani, asije akafa vitani na mtu mwingine akayafurahia.
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu aliyepanda shamba la mizabibu lakini bado hajala zabibu zake? Arudi nyumbani. La sivyo, anaweza kufa vitani, na mtu mwingine atazila.

decisions.choice: put to common use: first eat the vineyard's fruit as ordinary food
decisions.reason: The fruit of a new planting was not eaten for three years; the fourth year's fruit was holy to the LORD, and only from the fifth year could the owner eat it (Leviticus 19:23-25). The verb means to make something ordinary that was set apart, so a man who had waited all those years had not yet had the use of his vineyard. Jeremiah 31:5 uses the same verb. As in verse 5, losing the fruit of one's work is a covenant curse (28:30).

decisions.choice: enjoy its fruit / eaten its grapes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what putting a vineyard to use meant. Literal keeps the form of the verb, "put to common use".

source.text: וּמִֽי־הָאִ֞ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־אֵרַ֤שׂ אִשָּׁה֙ וְלֹ֣א לְקָחָ֔הּ יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ פֶּן־יָמוּת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאִ֥ישׁ אַחֵ֖ר יִקָּחֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And who [is] the man who has betrothed a woman and not taken her? Let him go and let him return to his house, lest he die in the battle and a man other take her.

en.L: And who [is] the man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.'
en.B: Has anyone become pledged to a woman and not yet married her? He should go back home, or he may die in battle and someone else marry her.'
en.R: Has any man promised to marry a woman but not yet married her? He should go back home. Otherwise he might die in the battle, and another man would marry her.'

es.L: ¿Y quién [es] el hombre que se ha desposado con una mujer y no la ha tomado? Que se vaya y vuelva a su casa, no sea que muera en la batalla y otro hombre la tome”.
es.B: ¿Hay alguien que se haya comprometido con una mujer y todavía no se haya casado con ella? Que vuelva a su casa, no sea que muera en la batalla y otro se case con ella”.
es.R: ¿Hay algún hombre que haya prometido casarse con una mujer y todavía no se haya casado con ella? Que regrese a su casa. Si no, podría morir en la batalla, y otro hombre se casaría con ella”.

fr.L: Et qui [est] l’homme qui s’est fiancé à une femme et ne l’a pas prise ? Qu’il s’en aille et retourne à sa maison, de peur qu’il ne meure au combat et qu’un autre homme ne la prenne.”
fr.B: Quelqu’un s’est-il engagé envers une femme sans l’avoir encore épousée ? Qu’il retourne chez lui, sinon il pourrait mourir au combat et un autre l’épouserait.”
fr.R: Y a-t-il un homme qui a promis d’épouser une femme mais ne l’a pas encore épousée ? Qu’il rentre chez lui. Sinon, il pourrait mourir dans la bataille, et un autre homme l’épouserait.”

sw.L: Na ni nani mtu aliyeposa mwanamke, naye hajamchukua? Aende, arudi nyumbani kwake, asije akafa vitani, na mtu mwingine akamchukua.'
sw.B: Je, kuna mtu aliyemchumbia mwanamke na bado hajamwoa? Arudi nyumbani, asije akafa vitani na mtu mwingine akamwoa.'
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu aliyeahidi kumwoa mwanamke lakini bado hajamwoa? Arudi nyumbani. La sivyo, anaweza kufa vitani, na mtu mwingine atamwoa.'

decisions.choice: betrothed: bound by a marriage agreement, not yet living together
decisions.reason: Betrothal was a binding agreement, sealed by the gift paid to the bride's family; the woman already counted as the man's wife in law (22:23-24), but she had not yet come to live in his house.

decisions.choice: take her: marry her, bring her into his home
decisions.reason: To "take" a woman is the usual way of saying "marry" (21:13; 24:1). The newly married man is likewise kept home for a year (24:5). The officials' words close at the end of this verse.

decisions.choice: pledged to / promised to marry; married
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid the older word "betrothed" and say "marry" for "take".

source.text: וְיָסְפ֣וּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים֮ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־הָעָם֒ וְאָמְר֗וּ מִי־הָאִ֤ישׁ הַיָּרֵא֙ וְרַ֣ךְ הַלֵּבָ֔ב יֵלֵ֖ךְ וְיָשֹׁ֣ב לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֛ס אֶת־לְבַ֥ב אֶחָ֖יו כִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall speak further the officials to the people and say, who [is] the man fearful and faint of heart? Let him go and let him return to his house, and not let melt the heart of his brothers like his heart.

en.L: And the officials shall speak further to the people and say, 'Who [is] the man [who is] afraid and faint of heart? Let him go and return to his house, so that the heart of his brothers does not melt like his heart.'
en.B: The officials are to go on to say to the troops, 'Is anyone afraid or fainthearted? He should go back home, so that he does not make his fellow soldiers lose heart as he has.'
en.R: Then the officials must also say, 'Is any man here afraid? Has he lost his courage? He should go back home. Otherwise the other soldiers will lose their courage too, just as he has.'

es.L: Y los funcionarios seguirán hablando al pueblo y dirán: “¿Quién [es] el hombre [que es] medroso y de corazón débil? Que se vaya y vuelva a su casa, para que no se derrita el corazón de sus hermanos como su corazón”.
es.B: Los funcionarios seguirán diciendo a las tropas: “¿Hay alguien que tenga miedo o le falte valor? Que vuelva a su casa, para que no haga perder el valor a sus compañeros como lo ha perdido él”.
es.R: Luego los funcionarios deben decir también: “¿Hay aquí algún hombre que tenga miedo? ¿Ha perdido el valor? Que regrese a su casa. Si no, los demás soldados también perderán el valor, como él”.

fr.L: Et les préposés parleront encore au peuple et diront : “Qui [est] l’homme [qui est] craintif et au cœur faible ? Qu’il s’en aille et retourne à sa maison, afin que le cœur de ses frères ne fonde pas comme son cœur.”
fr.B: Les préposés diront encore aux troupes : “Quelqu’un a-t-il peur ou manque-t-il de courage ? Qu’il retourne chez lui, pour ne pas faire perdre courage à ses compagnons d’armes comme lui.”
fr.R: Ensuite, les responsables doivent dire encore : “Y a-t-il ici un homme qui a peur ? A-t-il perdu courage ? Qu’il rentre chez lui. Sinon, les autres soldats perdront courage eux aussi, comme lui.”

sw.L: Na wasimamizi wataendelea kusema na watu, na kusema, 'Ni nani mtu [aliye] na hofu na moyo dhaifu? Aende, arudi nyumbani kwake, ili mioyo ya ndugu zake isiyeyuke kama moyo wake.'
sw.B: Wasimamizi waendelee kuwaambia wanajeshi, 'Je, kuna mtu mwenye hofu au aliyekata tamaa? Arudi nyumbani, ili asiwafanye wanajeshi wenzake wakate tamaa kama yeye.'
sw.R: Kisha lazima maafisa waseme pia, 'Je, kuna mtu hapa mwenye hofu? Je, amepoteza ujasiri? Arudi nyumbani. La sivyo, askari wengine nao watapoteza ujasiri, kama yeye.'

decisions.choice: let the heart melt: make others lose courage
decisions.reason: A melting heart is courage giving way (1:28; Joshua 2:11; 5:1). Fear spreads through an army, so the fearful man is sent home for the sake of the rest.

decisions.choice: the fearful man sent home: Gideon's army
decisions.reason: Gideon follows this rule when he sends home everyone who is afraid, and the LORD gives the victory to the few who remain (Judges 7:3).

decisions.choice: his brothers: his fellow Israelites in the army
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here are the other men of Israel standing in the ranks beside him (as in 1:16; 3:18).

decisions.choice: his fellow soldiers / the other soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the brothers by their place in the army. Those meant are the men called up to fight, so no inclusive wording is needed.

source.text: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּכַלֹּ֥ת הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־הָעָ֑ם וּפָֽקְד֛וּ שָׂרֵ֥י צְבָא֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it shall be, when finish the officials to speak to the people, and they shall appoint commanders of armies at [the] head of the people.

en.L: And it shall be, when the officials have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of armies at the head of the people.
en.B: When the officials have finished speaking to the troops, they are to appoint commanders of the divisions to lead them.
en.R: When the officials have finished talking to the soldiers, they must choose commanders to lead the army.

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando los funcionarios terminen de hablar al pueblo, pondrán comandantes de ejércitos a la cabeza del pueblo.
es.B: Cuando los funcionarios hayan terminado de hablar a las tropas, nombrarán comandantes de las divisiones para que las dirijan.
es.R: Cuando los funcionarios terminen de hablar a los soldados, deben elegir comandantes para dirigir el ejército.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, quand les préposés auront achevé de parler au peuple, qu’ils établiront des commandants d’armées à la tête du peuple.
fr.B: Quand les préposés auront fini de parler aux troupes, ils nommeront des commandants de divisions pour les conduire.
fr.R: Quand les responsables auront fini de parler aux soldats, ils doivent choisir des commandants pour diriger l’armée.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, wasimamizi watakapomaliza kusema na watu, wataweka makamanda wa majeshi juu ya watu.
sw.B: Wasimamizi watakapomaliza kusema na wanajeshi, wateue makamanda wa vikosi wawaongoze.
sw.R: Maafisa watakapomaliza kusema na askari, lazima wachague makamanda wa kuliongoza jeshi.

decisions.choice: commanders of armies: officers over the army's units
decisions.reason: The first word names a leader or officer; with "armies" it means the commanders of the companies into which the army was divided (1:15; Numbers 31:14, 48).

decisions.choice: they shall appoint: the officials appoint the commanders
decisions.reason: The subject is most naturally the officials who have just spoken. The verb could also be read without a fixed subject, "commanders shall be appointed"; the sense is the same: the army is put under its leaders only after it has been thinned out.

decisions.choice: commanders; divisions
decisions.reason: In a military setting the word for an officer is rendered "commanders" at every level, as Balanced does in 1:15. For the army's units Balanced uses "divisions", as in the camp lists of Numbers; Literal keeps "armies".

source.text: כִּֽי־תִקְרַ֣ב אֶל־עִ֔יר לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עָלֶ֑יהָ וְקָרָ֥אתָ אֵלֶ֖יהָ לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: When you draw near to a city to fight against it, and you shall call to it for peace.

en.L: When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call out to it for peace.
en.B: When you march up to a city to attack it, first offer it terms of peace.
en.R: When you go to attack a city, first offer to make peace with its people.

es.L: Cuando te acerques a una ciudad para combatir contra ella, la llamarás a la paz.
es.B: Cuando avances contra una ciudad para atacarla, ofrécele primero condiciones de paz.
es.R: Cuando vayas a atacar una ciudad, ofrece primero a sus habitantes hacer la paz.

fr.L: Quand tu t’approcheras d’une ville pour combattre contre elle, tu l’appelleras à la paix.
fr.B: Quand tu marcheras contre une ville pour l’attaquer, propose-lui d’abord des conditions de paix.
fr.R: Quand tu vas attaquer une ville, propose d’abord à ses habitants de faire la paix.

sw.L: Utakapoukaribia mji ili kupigana nao, utautangazia amani.
sw.B: Utakapoukaribia mji ili kuushambulia, kwanza uupe masharti ya amani.
sw.R: Unapokwenda kuushambulia mji, kwanza uwape watu wake nafasi ya kufanya amani nawe.

decisions.choice: call to it for peace: offer terms that would spare its people
decisions.reason: To call a city to peace is to offer it terms of surrender in place of battle. Moses did this with Sihon king of Heshbon (2:26), and the congregation used the same words to the men of Benjamin (Judges 21:13).

decisions.choice: a city: here, a city far from the land
decisions.reason: Verse 15 limits this rule to cities far away. The cities of the land Israel is entering are dealt with separately in verses 16-18.

decisions.choice: first; terms of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "first": the offer comes before any attack, as verses 11-12 show. Balanced adds "terms of" to show that peace is offered on conditions.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ אִם־שָׁל֣וֹם תַּֽעַנְךָ֔ וּפָתְחָ֖ה לָ֑ךְ וְהָיָ֞ה כָּל־הָעָ֣ם הַנִּמְצָא־בָ֗הּ יִהְי֥וּ לְךָ֛ לָמַ֖ס וַעֲבָדֽוּךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it shall be, if peace it answers you and it opens to you, and it shall be, all the people found in it shall become for you for forced labor and they shall serve you.

en.L: And it shall be, if it answers you [with] peace and opens to you, then all the people found in it shall become forced labor for you and shall serve you.
en.B: If it accepts your offer of peace and opens its gates to you, then all the people in it are to become forced laborers for you and serve you.
en.R: If its people agree to make peace and open their gates to you, they must all do forced labor for you and serve you.

es.L: Y sucederá que, si te responde [con] paz y se abre a ti, todo el pueblo que se encuentre en ella quedará para ti sujeto a trabajos forzados y te servirá.
es.B: Si acepta tu oferta de paz y te abre sus puertas, todos sus habitantes quedarán sujetos a trabajos forzados para ti y te servirán.
es.R: Si sus habitantes aceptan hacer la paz y te abren sus puertas, todos ellos tendrán que hacer trabajos forzados para ti y servirte.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, si elle te répond [par la] paix et s’ouvre à toi, que tout le peuple qui s’y trouve sera astreint pour toi à la corvée et te servira.
fr.B: Si elle accepte ton offre de paix et t’ouvre ses portes, alors tous ses habitants seront astreints à la corvée pour toi et te serviront.
fr.R: Si ses habitants acceptent de faire la paix et t’ouvrent leurs portes, ils devront tous faire des travaux forcés pour toi et te servir.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, ukikujibu [kwa] amani na kukufungulia, watu wote walioonekana ndani yake watakuwa kwako watu wa kazi ya kulazimishwa, nao watakutumikia.
sw.B: Mji ukikubali masharti yako ya amani na kukufungulia malango yake, watu wote waliomo watakufanyia kazi ya kulazimishwa na kukutumikia.
sw.R: Watu wake wakikubali kufanya amani na kukufungulia malango yao, lazima wote wakufanyie kazi ya kulazimishwa na kukutumikia.

decisions.choice: answers you with peace and opens to you: accepts the terms and surrenders
decisions.reason: To answer with peace is to accept the offer of verse 10. Opening to the besiegers means opening the city gates, giving up the city without a fight.

decisions.choice: forced labor: a work levy owed to the stronger power
decisions.reason: The word names a body of people made to work on the ruler's projects. Israel later made Canaanites do such work (Joshua 16:10; 1 Kings 9:21), and Israelites themselves were made to do it under Solomon (1 Kings 5:27).

decisions.choice: serve you: be subject to you
decisions.reason: Here serving means being a subject people under Israel, giving labor; it does not say the people of the city are bought or sold.

decisions.choice: its gates
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the city opens: its gates.

decisions.choice: astreint à la corvée (L, B); faire des travaux forcés (R)
decisions.reason: The word names a labor levy, work owed to the ruler (m2), not a payment; "corvée" is the French word for such a levy. Readable uses the plainer "travaux forcés".

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֤א תַשְׁלִים֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ וְעָשְׂתָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְצַרְתָּ֖ עָלֶֽיהָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not it makes peace with you and it makes with you war, and you shall besiege it.

en.L: But if it does not make peace with you, and makes war with you, then you shall besiege it.
en.B: But if it refuses to make peace with you and fights against you, lay siege to it.
en.R: But the city may refuse to make peace with you and decide to fight you instead. Then surround it and cut it off.

es.L: Pero si no hace la paz contigo y te hace la guerra, entonces la sitiarás.
es.B: Pero si se niega a hacer la paz contigo y te combate, ponle sitio.
es.R: Pero puede que la ciudad no quiera hacer la paz contigo y decida pelear contra ti. Entonces rodéala y no dejes que nadie entre ni salga.

fr.L: Mais si elle ne fait pas la paix avec toi et qu’elle te fait la guerre, alors tu l’assiégeras.
fr.B: Mais si elle refuse de faire la paix avec toi et te combat, assiège-la.
fr.R: Mais la ville peut refuser de faire la paix avec toi et décider plutôt de te combattre. Alors encercle-la, et que personne ne puisse y entrer ni en sortir.

sw.L: Lakini mji huo usipofanya amani nawe, ukafanya vita nawe, basi utauzingira.
sw.B: Lakini ukikataa kufanya amani nawe na kupigana nawe, uzingire.
sw.R: Lakini huenda watu wa mji wakakataa kufanya amani nawe, wakaamua kupigana nawe badala yake. Basi uuzunguke mji huo, usiruhusu mtu yeyote kuingia wala kutoka.

decisions.choice: make peace: accept the terms and come under Israel
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for peace. Used of a city it means to settle with an enemy by giving in to its terms (Joshua 10:1, 4; 11:19).

decisions.choice: besiege: surround the city and cut off its supplies
decisions.reason: A siege shut a walled city in until hunger or an attack on the walls forced it to fall. Verses 19-20 return to the siege.

decisions.choice: surround it and cut it off
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a siege is instead of using the word.

source.text: וּנְתָנָ֛הּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְהִכִּיתָ֥ אֶת־כָּל־זְכוּרָ֖הּ לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And shall give it Yahweh your God into your hand, and you shall strike every male of it by [the] mouth of [the] sword.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will give it into your hand, and you shall strike every male in it with the edge of the sword.
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God hands it over to you, put all its men to the sword.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will let you capture it. Then kill all the men in the city.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios la entregará en tu mano, y herirás a todo varón que haya en ella a filo de espada.
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te la entregue, pasa a todos sus hombres a filo de espada.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te permitirá conquistarla. Entonces mata a todos los hombres de la ciudad.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu la livrera entre tes mains, et tu frapperas tout mâle qui s’y trouve du tranchant de l’épée.
fr.B: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te l’aura livrée, passe tous ses hommes au fil de l’épée.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te permettra de la prendre. Alors tue tous les hommes de la ville.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atautia mkononi mwako, nawe utampiga kila mwanamume aliye ndani yake kwa makali ya upanga.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapoutia mikononi mwako, uwaue wanaume wake wote kwa upanga.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakuwezesha kuuteka. Kisha uwaue wanaume wote wa mji huo.

decisions.choice: give it into your hand: let you capture it
decisions.reason: The victory is the LORD's gift (verse 4; 2:24; 7:2). The city falls because he gives it, not by Israel's strength alone.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the sword: the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: The sword is pictured as a mouth that devours (32:42). The phrase means killing in battle.

decisions.choice: every male: the city's men, set against its women and little ones
decisions.reason: Verse 14 sets the women and the little ones apart, so "every male" here means the grown men, the city's fighting force. The command is narrower than the one for the cities of the land in verse 16.

decisions.choice: put to the sword / kill
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a common English phrase for killing with the sword; Readable says it plainly. Both say "men" for "males" (m3).

source.text: רַ֣ק הַ֠נָּשִׁים וְהַטַּ֨ף וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה בָעִ֛יר כָּל־שְׁלָלָ֖הּ תָּבֹ֣ז לָ֑ךְ וְאָֽכַלְתָּ֙ אֶת־שְׁלַ֣ל אֹיְבֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Only the women and the little ones and the livestock and all that is in the city, all its spoil, you shall plunder for yourself, and you shall eat [the] spoil of your enemies which has given Yahweh your God to you.

en.L: Only the women and the little ones and the livestock and all that is in the city, all its spoil, you shall take as plunder for yourself, and you shall eat the spoil of your enemies, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.
en.B: But the women, the children, the livestock and everything else in the city, all its spoil, you may carry off as plunder for yourselves. You may use the spoil of your enemies, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you.
en.R: But you may keep the women, the children, the animals and everything else in the city for yourselves. You may enjoy all that you take from your enemies. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given it to you.

es.L: Solo las mujeres y los niños pequeños y el ganado, y todo lo que haya en la ciudad, todo su botín, lo tomarás como despojo para ti, y comerás el botín de tus enemigos, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha dado.
es.B: Pero las mujeres, los niños, el ganado y todo lo demás que haya en la ciudad, todo su botín, podrás llevártelo para ti. Podrás aprovechar el botín de tus enemigos, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha dado.
es.R: Pero puedes quedarte con las mujeres, los niños, los animales y todo lo demás que haya en la ciudad. Puedes disfrutar de todo lo que tomes de tus enemigos. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te lo ha dado.

fr.L: Seulement, les femmes et les petits enfants et le bétail, et tout ce qui sera dans la ville, tout son butin, tu le pilleras pour toi, et tu mangeras le butin de tes ennemis, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a donné.
fr.B: Mais les femmes, les enfants, le bétail et tout le reste de ce qui se trouve dans la ville, tout son butin, tu peux l’emporter pour toi. Tu pourras profiter du butin de tes ennemis, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a donné.
fr.R: Mais tu peux garder pour toi les femmes, les enfants, les animaux et tout le reste de ce qui est dans la ville. Tu peux profiter de tout ce que tu prends à tes ennemis. C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu qui te l’a donné.

sw.L: Ila wanawake na watoto wadogo na mifugo, na vyote vilivyomo mjini, nyara zake zote, utazichukua kuwa nyara zako, nawe utakula nyara za adui zako, ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekupa.
sw.B: Lakini wanawake, watoto, mifugo na kila kitu kingine kilichomo mjini, nyara zake zote, unaweza kujichukulia. Unaweza kutumia nyara za adui zako, ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekupa.
sw.R: Lakini unaweza kujiwekea wanawake, watoto, wanyama na kila kitu kingine kilichomo mjini. Unaweza kufurahia vyote unavyowanyang'anya adui zako. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako amekupa.

decisions.choice: the women and the little ones: taken as captives into Israel
decisions.reason: The women and children were not killed but brought into Israelite households. A later law sets limits on how a captive woman is to be treated (21:10-14).

decisions.choice: eat the spoil: use and enjoy what was captured
decisions.reason: To "eat" here means to have the use of something, as in 6:11 and 28:33, not only to eat food.

decisions.choice: which the LORD your God has given you: the spoil is his gift
decisions.reason: Even the spoil is a gift. In the cities of the land, by contrast, the things devoted to the LORD were not to be kept (7:25-26; 13:18).

decisions.choice: use / enjoy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "eat" means here (m2). Literal keeps "eat".

source.text: כֵּ֤ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ לְכָל־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים הָרְחֹקֹ֥ת מִמְּךָ֖ מְאֹ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־מֵעָרֵ֥י הַגּֽוֹיִם־הָאֵ֖לֶּה הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus you shall do to all the cities far from you very, which not of [the] cities of the nations these they [are].

en.L: Thus you shall do to all the cities [that are] very far from you, which [are] not of the cities of these nations.
en.B: This is how you are to deal with all the cities that are very far from you, the ones that do not belong to the nations here.
en.R: Deal in this way with all the cities that are a long way from you. But this is not for the cities of the nations who live in the land you are entering.

es.L: Así harás a todas las ciudades [que están] muy lejos de ti, que no [son] de las ciudades de estas naciones.
es.B: Así tratarás a todas las ciudades que están muy lejos de ti, las que no pertenecen a las naciones de aquí.
es.R: Trata así a todas las ciudades que están lejos de ti. Pero esto no vale para las ciudades de las naciones que viven en la tierra donde vas a entrar.

fr.L: C’est ainsi que tu feras à toutes les villes [qui sont] très éloignées de toi, qui ne [sont] pas des villes de ces nations-ci.
fr.B: Voilà comment tu agiras envers toutes les villes qui sont très loin de toi, celles qui n’appartiennent pas aux nations d’ici.
fr.R: Agis ainsi avec toutes les villes qui sont loin de chez toi. Mais cela ne vaut pas pour les villes des nations qui vivent dans le pays où tu entres.

sw.L: Ndivyo utakavyoifanyia miji yote [iliyo] mbali sana nawe, ambayo si ya miji ya mataifa haya.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo utakavyoitendea miji yote iliyo mbali sana nawe, isiyo ya mataifa ya hapa.
sw.R: Itendee hivyo miji yote iliyo mbali nawe. Lakini hili si kwa miji ya mataifa wanaoishi katika nchi unayoingia.

decisions.choice: these nations: the nations of the land Israel is entering
decisions.reason: "These nations" are the peoples living in the land itself, named in verse 17 and in 7:1. The rule of verses 10-14 is for cities beyond them.

decisions.choice: the nations here
decisions.reason: Balanced says "here" for "these" to point to the land Israel is about to enter.

decisions.choice: who live in the land you are entering
decisions.reason: Readable says who "these nations" are, from verses 16-17.

source.text: רַ֗ק מֵעָרֵ֤י הָֽעַמִּים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָ֑ה לֹ֥א תְחַיֶּ֖ה כָּל־נְשָׁמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Only from [the] cities of the peoples these which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you [as] inheritance, not you shall let live any breath.

en.L: Only, of the cities of these peoples that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you [as] an inheritance, you shall not let live anything that breathes.
en.B: But in the cities of these peoples that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as an inheritance, do not leave alive anything that breathes.
en.R: But it is different with the cities in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to be your own. There you must not let anyone stay alive.

es.L: Solamente, de las ciudades de estos pueblos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da [como] heredad, no dejarás con vida nada que respire.
es.B: Pero en las ciudades de estos pueblos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da como heredad, no dejes con vida a ningún ser que respire.
es.R: Pero es distinto con las ciudades de la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da para que sea tuya. Allí no debes dejar a nadie con vida.

fr.L: Seulement, des villes de ces peuples que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne [en] héritage, tu ne laisseras vivre rien de ce qui respire.
fr.B: Mais dans les villes de ces peuples que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne en héritage, ne laisse en vie aucun être qui respire.
fr.R: Mais il en va autrement des villes du pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne pour qu’il soit à toi. Là, tu ne dois laisser personne en vie.

sw.L: Ila, katika miji ya watu hawa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa [kuwa] urithi, usiache hai chochote kinachopumua.
sw.B: Lakini katika miji ya watu hawa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa kuwa urithi, usiache hai kiumbe chochote kinachopumua.
sw.R: Lakini ni tofauti kwa miji ya nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa iwe yako. Huko usimwache mtu yeyote hai.

decisions.choice: anything that breathes: every person in those cities
decisions.reason: The word means breath, and so a living being. The same phrase is used in Joshua 10:40 and 11:11, 14; in 11:14 the people were killed but the livestock was kept, which shows that the phrase there means human beings. At Jericho the animals were included as well (Joshua 6:21).

decisions.choice: inheritance: land given as a lasting possession
decisions.reason: The land is Israel's inheritance: a share given by the LORD to be handed down in each family (4:21; 12:9).

decisions.choice: to be your own; anyone
decisions.reason: Readable says "to be your own" for "as an inheritance" and "anyone" for "anything that breathes", following m1.

source.text: כִּֽי־הַחֲרֵ֣ם תַּחֲרִימֵ֗ם הַחִתִּ֤י וְהָאֱמֹרִי֙ הַכְּנַעֲנִ֣י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: But devoting to destruction you shall devote them to destruction, the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, as has commanded you Yahweh your God,

en.L: But you shall utterly devote them to destruction, the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you,
en.B: You must devote them completely to destruction, the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you,
en.R: You must destroy them completely, as people given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you.

es.L: Sino que los consagrarás por completo a la destrucción: al hitita y al amorreo, al cananeo y al ferezeo, al heveo y al jebuseo, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha mandado,
es.B: Deberás consagrarlos por completo a la destrucción, a los hititas, amorreos, cananeos, ferezeos, heveos y jebuseos, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te mandó,
es.R: Tendrás que destruirlos por completo, como pueblos entregados {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: los hititas, amorreos, cananeos, ferezeos, heveos y jebuseos. Esto es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te ha mandado.

fr.L: Mais tu les voueras entièrement à la destruction, le Hittite et l’Amoréen, le Cananéen et le Phérézien, l’Hévien et le Jébusien, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te l’a ordonné,
fr.B: Tu dois les vouer entièrement à la destruction, les Hittites, les Amoréens, les Cananéens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te l’a ordonné,
fr.R: Tu dois les détruire complètement, comme des peuples donnés {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : les Hittites, les Amoréens, les Cananéens, les Phéréziens, les Héviens et les Jébusiens. C’est ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a ordonné.

sw.L: Bali hakika utawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, Mhiti na Mwamori, Mkanaani na Mperizi, Mhivi na Myebusi, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alivyokuamuru,
sw.B: Lazima uwaweke wakfu kabisa kwa maangamizi, Wahiti, Waamori, Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi, kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alivyokuamuru,
sw.R: Lazima uwaangamize kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: Wahiti, Waamori, Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi. Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alivyokuamuru.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give over wholly to the LORD by destroying
decisions.reason: As in 7:2: what is devoted is taken out of human use and given over to the LORD for good, so nothing is kept for gain. The verb is doubled for emphasis.

decisions.choice: the ban on the peoples of the land: limited to this land, and grounded in its worship
decisions.reason: This is one of the hardest commands in Scripture; the note at 7:2 sets out what Deuteronomy itself says about its limits and reasons. In this chapter the contrast is sharp: cities far away are first offered peace (verses 10-15), but the ban falls on the peoples of the land, and verse 18 gives the reason: they would teach Israel to serve their gods. The verse states the command as it was given; it does not by itself settle how fully it was carried out or how its strong language of war is to be weighed.

decisions.choice: six peoples, without the Girgashites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text names six peoples; 7:1 names seven, adding the Girgashites. The ancient Greek translation adds the Girgashites here too, to match the fuller list. The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: destroy them completely, as people given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 7:2, Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction". Readable ends the sentence here and begins verse 18 with a new one.

source.text: לְמַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יְלַמְּד֤וּ אֶתְכֶם֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּכֹל֙ תּֽוֹעֲבֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ לֵֽאלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַחֲטָאתֶ֖ם לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: so that not they teach you to do according to all their abominations which they have done for their gods, and you sin against Yahweh your God.

en.L: so that they may not teach you to do according to all their abominations which they have done for their gods, and you sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.
en.B: so that they will not teach you to copy all the detestable practices they have carried out for their gods, and so lead you to sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.
en.R: Otherwise they would teach you to do all the disgusting things they do to worship their gods, and you would sin against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

es.L: para que no {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñen a hacer conforme a todas sus abominaciones que han hecho para sus dioses, y {{plural_you:pequen|pequéis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.
es.B: para que no {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñen a imitar todas las prácticas detestables que realizan para sus dioses, y así {{plural_you:los|os}} lleven a pecar contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.
es.R: Si no, {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñarían a hacer todas las cosas repugnantes que hacen para adorar a sus dioses, y {{plural_you:ustedes pecarían|vosotros pecaríais}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.

fr.L: afin qu’ils ne vous enseignent pas à faire selon toutes leurs abominations qu’ils ont faites pour leurs dieux, et que vous ne péchiez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.
fr.B: pour qu’ils ne vous apprennent pas à imiter toutes les pratiques détestables qu’ils accomplissent pour leurs dieux, et qu’ainsi vous ne péchiez pas contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.
fr.R: Sinon, ils vous apprendraient à faire toutes les choses dégoûtantes qu’ils font pour adorer leurs dieux, et vous pécheriez contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu.

sw.L: ili wasiwafundishe kutenda kama machukizo yao yote waliyoifanyia miungu yao, nanyi mkamtenda dhambi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.
sw.B: ili wasiwafundishe kuiga desturi zao zote za kuchukiza wanazozifanya kwa ajili ya miungu yao, na hivyo kuwafanya mtende dhambi dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.
sw.R: La sivyo, wangewafundisha kufanya mambo yote ya kuchukiza wanayoyafanya ili kuabudu miungu yao, nanyi mngetenda dhambi dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.

decisions.choice: abominations: practices the LORD finds abhorrent
decisions.reason: The word is used for what the LORD cannot bear, above all the worship of other gods and the burning of children in that worship (12:31; 18:9-12).

decisions.choice: so that they may not teach you: the reason is worship
decisions.reason: The reason given for the ban is the danger to Israel's faith: living among these peoples, Israel would learn their worship (7:4; 12:29-31). It is not hatred of a people as such; an Israelite town that turns to other gods falls under the same ban (13:13-19).

decisions.choice: and you sin: the result that would follow
decisions.reason: The last clause says what their teaching would lead to: Israel sinning against the LORD.

decisions.choice: detestable practices / disgusting things they do to worship
decisions.reason: Balanced says "detestable" for the older "abominations", as in 17:1; Readable uses a plainer word and says that these things were done in worship.

source.text: כִּֽי־תָצ֣וּר אֶל־עִיר֩ יָמִ֨ים רַבִּ֜ים לְֽהִלָּחֵ֧ם עָלֶ֣יהָ לְתָפְשָׂ֗הּ לֹֽא־תַשְׁחִ֤ית אֶת־עֵצָהּ֙ לִנְדֹּ֤חַ עָלָיו֙ גַּרְזֶ֔ן כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ תֹאכֵ֔ל וְאֹת֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִכְרֹ֑ת כִּ֤י הָֽאָדָם֙ עֵ֣ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָבֹ֥א מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בַּמָּצֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: When you besiege a city many days, to fight against it to capture it, not you shall destroy its tree[s] by swinging against it an ax, for from it you shall eat, and it not you shall cut down; for [is] the man the tree of the field, to go before you in the siege?

en.L: When you besiege a city many days, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by swinging an ax against them, for you may eat from them, and you shall not cut them down. For is the tree of the field a man, to go in before you under siege?
en.B: When you besiege a city for a long time, fighting against it to take it, do not destroy its trees by taking an ax to them. You may eat their fruit; do not cut them down. Is a tree in the field a person, that you should besiege it as well?
en.R: You may have to surround a city for a long time as you fight to capture it. Even then, do not destroy its fruit trees by chopping them down with an ax. You can eat their fruit, so do not cut them down. Trees are not people. They are not the enemy you are fighting.

es.L: Cuando sities una ciudad muchos días, combatiendo contra ella para tomarla, no destruirás sus árboles blandiendo contra ellos el hacha, porque de ellos podrás comer, y no los cortarás. ¿Es acaso un hombre el árbol del campo, para entrar delante de ti en el asedio?
es.B: Cuando sities una ciudad durante mucho tiempo, combatiendo contra ella para conquistarla, no destruyas sus árboles metiéndoles el hacha. Podrás comer de su fruto; no los cortes. ¿Es acaso una persona el árbol del campo, para que también lo sities?
es.R: Puede que tengas que rodear una ciudad durante mucho tiempo mientras luchas por conquistarla. Aun así, no destruyas sus árboles frutales cortándolos con el hacha. Puedes comer su fruto, así que no los cortes. Los árboles no son personas. No son el enemigo contra el que peleas.

fr.L: Quand tu assiégeras une ville de nombreux jours, en combattant contre elle pour la prendre, tu ne détruiras pas ses arbres en levant contre eux la hache, car tu pourras en manger, et tu ne les abattras pas. Car l’arbre des champs est-il un homme, pour venir devant toi dans le siège ?
fr.B: Quand tu assiégeras une ville pendant longtemps, en la combattant pour t’en emparer, ne détruis pas ses arbres en y portant la hache. Tu pourras manger de leurs fruits ; ne les abats pas. L’arbre des champs est-il un homme, pour que tu l’assièges, lui aussi ?
fr.R: Il se peut que tu doives encercler une ville longtemps pour la prendre. Même alors, ne détruis pas ses arbres fruitiers en les abattant à la hache. Tu peux manger leurs fruits, alors ne les coupe pas. Les arbres ne sont pas des gens. Ils ne sont pas l’ennemi que tu combats.

sw.L: Utakapouzingira mji siku nyingi, ukipigana nao ili kuuteka, usiiharibu miti yake kwa kuipiga shoka, kwa maana utakula matunda yake, wala usiikate. Kwani je, mti wa shambani ni mtu, hata uingie mbele yako katika kuzingirwa?
sw.B: Utakapouzingira mji kwa muda mrefu, ukipigana nao ili kuuteka, usiiharibu miti yake kwa kuipiga shoka. Unaweza kula matunda yake; usiikate. Je, mti wa shambani ni mtu, hata nao uuzingire?
sw.R: Huenda ikakubidi kuuzunguka mji kwa muda mrefu unapopigana ili kuuteka. Hata hivyo, usiiharibu miti yake ya matunda kwa kuikata kwa shoka. Unaweza kula matunda yake, kwa hiyo usiikate. Miti si watu. Si adui unayepigana naye.

decisions.choice: is the tree of the field a man, to come before you in the siege?: a question expecting "no"
alternatives: for the man [is] the tree of the field
for a man's life [is] the tree of the field
decisions.reason: The vowels of the Hebrew text read the first word as a question: trees are not enemy soldiers, that they should be besieged and destroyed with the city. Read without the question, the words say "for the man [is] the tree of the field", which has been taken to mean that human life depends on such trees. Both readings lead to the same command: the trees that feed people are to be spared.

decisions.choice: do not destroy its trees: a limit on the ruin of war
decisions.reason: Armies besieging a city often cut down its orchards, both for timber and to ruin the land for years (2 Kings 3:19, 25). Moses forbids this for fruit trees, which feed people long after the war (verse 20).

decisions.choice: swinging an ax against it
decisions.reason: The verb means to drive or swing; it is used of a man swinging an ax at a tree in 19:5.

decisions.choice: from it you may eat: permission
decisions.reason: The verb can say what Israel will do or what it may do. Here it gives permission: the besiegers may eat the fruit, but not destroy the trees.

decisions.choice: fruit trees
decisions.reason: Readable says "fruit trees", since the verse speaks of trees whose fruit is eaten and verse 20 sets other trees apart.

decisions.choice: Trees are not people. They are not the enemy you are fighting.
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects (m1) instead of asking it.

source.text: רַ֞ק עֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר־תֵּדַ֗ע כִּֽי־לֹא־עֵ֤ץ מַאֲכָל֙ ה֔וּא אֹת֥וֹ תַשְׁחִ֖ית וְכָרָ֑תָּ וּבָנִ֣יתָ מָצ֗וֹר עַל־הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁר־הִ֨וא עֹשָׂ֧ה עִמְּךָ֛ מִלְחָמָ֖ה עַ֥ד רִדְתָּֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Only a tree that you know that not a tree of food it [is], it you may destroy and cut down, and you shall build siege works against the city which it [is] making with you war, until its going down.

en.L: Only a tree that you know is not a tree for food, it you may destroy and cut down, and you shall build siege works against the city that is making war with you, until it falls.
en.B: Only the trees that you know do not give food may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works against the city that is at war with you, until it falls.
en.R: But you may cut down trees that you know do not give food. Use them to build ramps and towers to attack the city that is fighting you, until it is defeated.

es.L: Solo el árbol que sepas que no es árbol [que da] alimento, ese podrás destruirlo y cortarlo, y construirás obras de asedio contra la ciudad que te hace la guerra, hasta que caiga.
es.B: Solo los árboles que sepas que no dan alimento podrás destruir y cortar, para construir obras de asedio contra la ciudad que está en guerra contigo, hasta que caiga.
es.R: Pero puedes cortar los árboles que sepas que no dan alimento. Úsalos para construir rampas y torres para atacar la ciudad que pelea contra ti, hasta que sea derrotada.

fr.L: Seulement, l’arbre dont tu sauras que ce n’est pas un arbre [qui donne] de la nourriture, celui-là tu pourras le détruire et l’abattre, et tu bâtiras des ouvrages de siège contre la ville qui te fait la guerre, jusqu’à ce qu’elle tombe.
fr.B: Seuls les arbres dont tu sais qu’ils ne donnent pas de nourriture, tu pourras les détruire et les abattre, pour bâtir des ouvrages de siège contre la ville qui est en guerre contre toi, jusqu’à ce qu’elle tombe.
fr.R: Mais tu peux couper les arbres dont tu sais qu’ils ne donnent pas de nourriture. Sers-t’en pour construire des rampes et des tours pour attaquer la ville qui te combat, jusqu’à ce qu’elle soit vaincue.

sw.L: Ila mti utakaoujua kwamba si mti wa chakula, huo unaweza kuuharibu na kuukata, nawe utajenga ngome za kuzingira juu ya mji unaofanya vita nawe, hadi utakapoanguka.
sw.B: Ni miti tu unayoijua kwamba haitoi chakula unayoweza kuiharibu na kuikata, ili kujenga ngome za kuuzingira mji ulio vitani nawe, hadi utakapoanguka.
sw.R: Lakini unaweza kukata miti unayoijua kwamba haitoi chakula. Itumie kujenga vilima na minara ya kuushambulia mji unaopigana nawe, hadi utakaposhindwa.

decisions.choice: a tree for food: a tree that bears fruit people eat
decisions.reason: The rule turns on what a tree is for. Trees that do not bear food may be used for the war; those that feed people are spared (verse 19).

decisions.choice: siege works: ramps, walls and towers built against a city
decisions.reason: The word is the one for "siege" in verse 19. Here it means the works an army built from earth and timber to shut a city in and reach its walls (2 Kings 25:1; Ezekiel 4:2).

decisions.choice: until its going down: until it falls
decisions.reason: The verb means to go down. Used of a city it means its fall, as of high walls coming down in 28:52.

decisions.choice: ramps and towers to attack
decisions.reason: Readable describes the siege works instead of using the term (m2).

decisions.choice: may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the building to the cutting, since the wood is cut for the siege works; the Hebrew joins them with "and".
